lessons.title: Vowels 1: অ আ
lessons.goal: Read the first two vowel letters, অ and আ, and words that start with them.
lessons.tip:
**Bengali has 11 vowel letters (স্বরবর্ণ *shorborno*).** They stand alone when a vowel *starts* a syllable, e.g. at the start of a word. Here are the first two:

- **অ** = `o`, a short open 'o' as in *or*. Every consonant secretly carries this sound, so you will see it everywhere later.
- **আ** = `a` as in *father*. It is অ plus an extra stick (া), and that stick is exactly the sign that adds 'a' to a consonant later.

Both hang from a top line (মাত্রা *matra*), which is how Bengali letters join into words. Like an alphabet chart, each letter comes with words that start with it: **অ**জগর, **আ**ম.

lessons.title: Vowels 1b: ই ঈ
lessons.goal: Read the two i-letters, ই and ঈ, and words that start with them.
lessons.tip:
**ই** and **ঈ** are both `i` as in *see*. Their names are 'short i' (ই) and 'long i' (ঈ), but **in everyday speech they sound the same**. You just learn which one each word is spelled with:

- **ই**লিশ (hilsa), **ই**ট (brick)
- **ঈ**গল (eagle), **ঈ**দ (Eid)

Because they sound alike, you will only ever tell them apart by sight, never by ear.

*Culture:* ইলিশ is Bangladesh's national fish, and ঈদ is one of the biggest holidays of the year.

lessons.title: Vowels 2: উ ঊ
lessons.goal: Read the two u-letters, উ and ঊ, and words that start with them.
lessons.tip:
**উ** and **ঊ** are both `u` as in *food*: a 'short u' and a 'long u' that **sound the same** in speech, just like ই and ঈ. The long **ঊ** has one more stroke.

Learn the spelling with the word:

- **উ**ট (camel), **উ**কিল (lawyer)
- **ঊ**রু (thigh), **ঊ**ষা (dawn)

ঊ is rare at the start of a word, so these are two of the few you'll see.

Watch out: উ looks a lot like the consonant ড (`d`) that you'll meet later; ড has a notch in its top line.

lessons.title: Vowels 2b: ঋ এ
lessons.goal: Read ঋ and এ and words that start with them.
lessons.tip:
- **ঋ** is said `ri` as in *rip*. It mostly appears in words borrowed from Sanskrit, like **ঋ**তু (season) and **ঋ**ষি (sage).
- **এ** = `e`. It has two sounds: an open 'a' as in *cat* (**এ**ক `ek`, one; **এ**খন `ekhon`, now) or 'ay' as in *say* (এই `ei`, this). You learn which by listening.

*Culture:* Bengal traditionally counts six seasons (ছয় ঋতু), not four.

lessons.title: Vowels 3: ঐ ও ঔ + review
lessons.tip:
The last three vowels are built from shapes you know:

- **ঐ** = `oi` as in *boy*. It is এ with a flick on top.
- **ও** = `o` as in *go*: rounder and more closed than **অ** (`o` as in *or*). Both are written `o` in transliteration, so trust your ears and the letter shape.
- **ঔ** = `ou` as in *low*. It is ও with a squiggle on top.

**All 11 vowels:** অ আ ই ঈ উ ঊ ঋ এ ঐ ও ঔ. Remember: ই/ঈ sound the same, and so do উ/ঊ.

Some example words here contain joined letters you haven't learned yet (like ক্য in ঐক্য); just recognise them as whole words for now. Fun fact: ওষুধ (everyday) and ঔষধ (formal) both mean *medicine*.
